history.title: Monolith-Split-Cost

style_when: the story is a product, a device, a price or a market for a thing the reader could buy — an appliance, a panel, a router, a robot arm
prompt: Studio product photograph of a heavy, unified brushed-steel industrial manifold with one distinct, highly polished titanium module physically detached from the main housing, resting heavily on a precision brass balance scale. Asymmetric off-centre composition on the right thirds with generous editorial negative space on the left. Shot with a 100mm lens, softbox key light casting a long, deliberate contact shadow across a textured matte slate surface. Clean catalogue clarity, deep material contrast between the dark steel monolith and the bright detached module, modern premium B2B editorial aesthetic.
negative_prompt: garbled text, random lettering, watermarks, UI, people, abstract floating shapes, gradient sweep, text, logos, blueprint, drawing
rationale: A studio object treatment isolates the exact economic trade-off at the heart of the story. By presenting a complex mechanical assembly being weighed and divided, it visually captures the heavy, tangible cost of splitting a unified architecture into modular parts.
cue: Splitting your monolith now has a price tag
subject: a heavy brushed-steel industrial manifold with one detached titanium module resting on a precision scale
core_thesis: Splitting a monolithic system into microservices incurs a 20% development cost premium but slows technical debt growth by 90%, making it viable only when the debt savings outweigh the build costs.
core_conflict: The high upfront cost and operational overhead of distributed microservices versus the slow-growing technical debt of a monolithic architecture.
